learning_objective: 🎯 Learn the precise format of drafting a formal Notice to convey information clearly to a target audience within a strict word limit.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A Notice MUST always be enclosed in a BOX. The standard format (Top to Bottom): Name of Issuing Agency/School, the word 'NOTICE' (in capital letters), Date (e.g., 15 March 2024), Heading/Subject, Body of the Notice, Signature, Name, and Designation.

A perfect notice answers 5 questions: WHAT is happening (Event), WHEN it is happening (Date & Time), WHERE it is happening (Venue), WHO can participate/attend (Target Audience), and WHOM to contact for further details.

The word limit is strictly 50 words (excluding the format). The tone must be formal, objective, and polite. Do not use personal pronouns like 'I' or 'We'. Instead of 'I am informing you', write 'This is to inform all students...'.

fun_activity.title: 🕵️‍♂️ The Missing Bottle Notice
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you lost your blue Milton water bottle in the school playground. Write the 'Body' of the notice in just 3 sentences! Mention: 1. What is lost. 2. Where & When. 3. Who to return it to. Keep it under 30 words!

exam_tips: 📌 NEVER fold or draw the bottom line of your Box until you have finished writing the entire notice! This keeps your presentation neat.
📌 Do not write 'Date:' before the date. Just write '24 October 2024'.
📌 For 'Lost and Found' notices, always promise a suitable reward for the finder to make it realistic.
quick_recap: ⭐ Marks are divided into: Format (1 Mark), Content (2 Marks), and Expression/Accuracy (1 Mark).
⭐ The word 'NOTICE' must always be in BLOCK/CAPITAL letters.
⭐ Always mention the deadline (Last Date) if the notice requires students to submit names or money.
